description: Confirm local zoning allows a data center
File conditional use or special exception application
Begin first hearing
source: MPC §908(1.2), applied to conditional use via §913.2
note: Conditional use borrows the zoning hearing board hearing rule.

description: Issue written decision (deemed approved if missed)
note: Deemed approval is the issue in the Muncy Township case. Archbald Borough Council denied the Wildcat Ridge conditional use application 7–0 on Oct. 21, 2026, after nine hearings; an appeal is expected (as reported).

description: File land development plan
Review plan and report to municipality
source: MPC §502(b), per MPC timing provisions summary
note: The municipality may not approve until it receives the county report or 30 days pass. Where a township has no subdivision ordinance of its own, the county ordinance applies.

description: Decide land development plan
time: Within 90 days after next regular meeting after filing
note: Written decision to applicant within 15 days after the decision.

description: Decision: sign a Consent Order and Agreement? (projects over 25 MW)
Yes: file notice of intent to meet GRID Requirements; meet with DEP on local approval timing; sign the order
Yes: review permits on a rolling basis; issue only after local approvals are documented
time: Permit clocks start after local approvals are documented

description: No: don't begin review until local approvals are documented
time: No rolling review; excluded from PAyback and Permit Decision Guarantee

description: Submit permit applications (stormwater, waterway encroachment, air plan approval for generators, as applicable)
source: General DEP permitting; the order names no specific permits
note: Labeled "as applicable."

description: Public notice and comment; hearing if scheduled
Issue permits
Request service; utility studies load and registers it with PJM
note: Runs alongside steps 1–13.

description: Large-load tariff rules: proposed, final PUC vote targeted Jan. 28, 2027
note: Runs alongside steps 1–13.

description: Confirm local zoning: by right, special use permit, or rezoning needed
note: Varies by locality. Loudoun ended by-right data centers in March 2025; Prince William largely did on Sept. 22, 2026. In October 2026, Amazon withdrew an 800,000 sq ft proposal at the former GWU campus in Ashburn after county staff found data centers were not a permitted primary use there; Amazon agreed to dedicate about 25 acres to the county and forgo legal action (as reported).

description: File rezoning, proffer amendment or special use permit application
Facilities of 100 MW or more: submit site assessment, including sound profile for homes and schools within 500 feet; utility discloses substations and transmission needed
note: Required before approval of a rezoning, proffer amendment or special use permit.

description: Public hearing and recommendation
time: Within 100 days after first meeting following referral
note: If the commission misses the deadline, it is deemed to have recommended approval. The project itself is not deemed approved.

description: Public hearing and decision
lane: Locality (board of supervisors or city council)
time: Within 12 months of submission, unless the applicant agrees to extend
note: Applies in counties. The statute sets no deemed approval if the deadline is missed; the applicant may agree to a longer period.

description: Submit site plan; locality acts
note: A resubmitted plan not acted on within 30 days is deemed approved. If a first review is late, the applicant may petition circuit court after 10 days' notice.

description: State review: projects of 25 MW or more get no expedited review
source: Executive Order 22 (Sept. 18, 2026), as reported by Holland & Knight
note: No state step waits on local approval, unlike Pennsylvania.

description: Air permit for backup generators: new data centers must use Tier 4 generators
source: 2026 session, as reported by Canary Media (June 23, 2026) and Data Center Knowledge
note: Applies to air permit applications from July 1, 2026 (as reported). The rest of HB 507 (batteries first, runtime caps) did not become law. DEQ guidance sets a presumptive limit of 0.60 g/hp-hr.

description: Other permits as applicable (construction stormwater, water withdrawal)
note: Eastern Virginia Groundwater Management Area designated a cooling-water-scarcity area.

description: Issue permits
Request service; utility identifies substations and transmission needed
note: Runs alongside steps 1–10. Feeds the step 3 site assessment.

description: Large-load rate class (GS-5) for customers of 25 MW or more: minimum 85% of transmission and distribution demand, 60% of generation demand
source: SCC final order, Dominion biennial review (Nov. 25, 2025), as reported by Loudoun Now

description: Transmission built for a data center is paid for by the data center
source: SCC order in Dominion's Rider T1 transmission case, early August 2026, as reported by Virginia Mercury and DCD
note: Dominion must develop a tariff that directly assigns transmission built for large-load customers to them; expected to take effect early 2027 (as reported). Case number not found.

description: Pending: 2027 session proposals to end by-right approval for data centers over 25 MW; moratorium bills filed
lane: Locality (board of supervisors or city council)
source: Governor's Data Center Accountability Framework; SB 843 (2027)
note: Loudoun voted Sept. 15, 2026 to move toward a pause of up to 12 months on data center applications.

description: Check local zoning: city (home rule), zoned township, or unzoned township
note: Where a township has adopted no zoning, there may be no local land use approval at all.

description: Decision: rezoning or conditional use needed?
note: Unzoned: skip to step 11.

description: File zoning amendment application
Send amendment to county or regional planning commission
lane: Township zoning commission, BZA & county planning commission
note: Planning commission recommendation is considered at the zoning commission hearing.

description: Public hearing
lane: Township zoning commission, BZA & county planning commission

description: Recommend approval, denial or modification to trustees
lane: Township zoning commission, BZA & county planning commission

description: Public hearing
Adopt, deny or modify
Rezoning takes effect unless voters petition for a referendum
time: 30 days after adoption; petition due within 30 days; vote at next election at least 90 days out
note: New (J)(1): megaproject rezonings take effect immediately with no referendum. The current megaproject definition (R.C. 122.17(A)(11)) does not exclude data centers, so a project meeting its $1 billion investment or $75 million payroll test and wage test could qualify. Pending HB 646 would exclude data centers from the main route.

description: Alternative: conditional use from the township board of zoning appeals
lane: Township zoning commission, BZA & county planning commission
note: Timelines set by each township's zoning resolution.

description: Apply for permits as applicable: air permit-to-install for backup generators; construction stormwater (over 1 acre); wastewater permits
source: Ohio EPA testimony, House Data Centers Committee, May 27, 2026
note: "Data centers are not subject to a unique environmental permitting program in Ohio."

description: Draft permit, public notice, comment period, hearing if requested or required, response to comments, final permit
note: Testimony does not tie Ohio EPA review to local zoning.

description: Draft general NPDES permit for data centers
note: Thousands of comments received.

description: Request service; AEP Ohio data center tariff for 25 MW and up: minimum demand up to 85% of contract capacity; contract of up to 4 ramp years plus 8 years
lane: Electric utility, PUCO & Power Siting Board
source: AEP Ohio tariff page; PUCO Case 24-508-EL-ATA (order July 9, 2025)
note: Applies to new facilities and expansions. HB 706 would extend similar terms to other utilities (introduced).

description: On-site power plant that is a major utility facility: Power Siting Board certificate replaces local review
lane: Electric utility, PUCO & Power Siting Board
source: Ohio Rev. Code 4906.13(B); HB 15 (2025); City of Hilliard
note: Hilliard: Ohio Power Company's 72.9 MW fuel cell plant for an AWS data center (Case 25-0649-EL-BLN) was filed as an accelerated application subject to automatic approval; staff recommended approval Sept. 22, 2025, and city review was withdrawn.

description: Check county zoning and any data center pause
note: Prince George's adopted a two-year pause in July 2026; Montgomery, Frederick and Baltimore County also paused development (as reported).

description: File rezoning, special exception or site plan under the county code
note: Each county sets its own procedures and timelines.

description: Review, hearing and recommendation or decision
lane: County planning board or board of appeals

description: Decide rezoning or zoning text amendment
note: Frederick County: a referendum petition on the January 2026 data center ordinance gathered more than 20,000 signatures, but a circuit court ruled June 18 that the zoning ordinance is not subject to referendum under the county charter, and the Maryland Supreme Court upheld that ruling June 30. It is not on the November ballot (as reported).

description: Decision: for projects of 25 MW or more seeking any state action, Task Force determination: Aligned, Conditionally Aligned or Not Aligned
Aligned or Conditionally Aligned: coordinated state review runs concurrently with local permitting; eligible for incentives
Not Aligned or no review: substantive state review deferred until local land-use approvals are documented; no discretionary incentives or state support
Decision: does backup generation qualify for the exclusion from state power plant approval?
source: SB 474 (2024), Critical Infrastructure Streamlining Act; Dept. of Legislative Services fiscal note
note: Qualifies if used only for emergency backup and testing, cannot send power to the grid, holds an MDE permit to construct, and meets noise and testing-hour rules.

description: Yes: permit to construct for backup generators; no PSC approval needed
source: SB 474 (2024), Critical Infrastructure Streamlining Act; Dept. of Legislative Services fiscal note
note: Owners report each use to MDE every Dec. 1; reports are public.

description: No: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (or PSC-approved exemption) for generation
note: Before 2024, the PSC capped one data center campus at 70 MW of backup generation.

description: Other permits as applicable (water appropriation, erosion and sediment control, stormwater)
note: Erosion and sediment control plans are approved by soil conservation districts, county or city public works departments, or MDE, depending on the jurisdiction.

description: Issue permits
Register with the Public Service Commission's large-load registry (energy and water use; fee of at least $1,000 per MW of peak load)
source: Mintz, AG Watch (Oct. 2026); Spotlight PA; T&D World (June 15, 2026)
note: Registration is with the PSC (as reported).

description: Request service; large-load customer rules apply at 25 MW and 60% load factor
source: HB 1532 (2026), Ch. 353, Utility RELIEF Act, as reported by Mintz
note: Emergency law lowered the 2025 threshold of 100 MW and 80% load factor. PJM capacity costs are passed through to large-load customers.

description: Large-load tariffs: utilities filed by Sept. 1, 2026; PSC review under way
Check county or city zoning for a data center use
note: Counties and cities each zone under their own ordinances.

description: Decision: is the project a Development of Regional Impact?
source: DCA board vote, Nov. 2025, as reported by Georgia Recorder
note: Data centers of 500,000 sq ft or more; 300,000 sq ft in urban and suburban areas of the Atlanta region.

description: Yes: submit project for regional review, with estimated water and electricity needs
source: DCA board vote, Nov. 2025, as reported by Georgia Recorder
note: Developer supplies the water and power estimates.

description: Review and comment; public notice
time: No more than 30 calendar days, unless extended
source: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 110-12-7-.01; DCA board vote, Nov. 2025
note: "The local government may not take final action approving the project while the DRI process is ongoing." Regional commissions comment but do not approve or oppose.

description: File rezoning or special use application
Review and recommendation
note: Where the locality has a planning commission.

description: Public hearing
time: Published notice 15 to 45 days before; sign on property at least 15 days before
note: Each side gets at least 10 minutes (§ 36-66-5).

description: Decide rezoning
note: If denied, the same property cannot be reconsidered for at least six months.

description: Permits as applicable: construction stormwater general permit (Notice of Intent to EPD); air permits for backup generators (permit-by-rule, synthetic minor or Title V, by size); pretreatment permit for significant industrial users
source: City of Tyrone data center information sheet
note: Synthetic minor permits are common for large generator fleets.

description: Issue permits
Request service; customers over 100 MW: contracts up to 15 years, minimum bills, and contracts submitted to the PSC for review
source: Georgia PSC media advisory, Jan. 23, 2025 (from Docket 55378)
note: Data centers pay site-specific costs and upstream generation, transmission and distribution costs as construction proceeds.
